name: Dr Amy Chen
bio: Amy has worked in general practice for 12 years and sees many young adults with ADHD. She splits her week between the New Farm clinic and telehealth.

evidence.excerpt: About a third of my patients are young adults with ADHD.
evidence.patientFacing: Amy has a particular interest in adult ADHD and sees many patients aged 18 to 35.

evidence.excerpt: Sleep comes up with nearly every ADHD patient, so I always ask about it.
evidence.patientFacing: Amy regularly treats sleep problems alongside ADHD.

evidence.excerpt: I do a lot of mental health care plans and follow-up.
evidence.patientFacing: Amy manages anxiety and low mood as part of ongoing care.

evidence.excerpt: I also do a lot of women's health.
evidence.patientFacing: Amy provides women's health care including contraception and hormonal health.

evidence.excerpt: I book 30 minutes for new patients and keep the last five for what happens next.
evidence.patientFacing: Amy books 30-minute first appointments and keeps the end of each visit to agree on next steps.
evidence.scenario: Walk me through a first appointment with a new patient.

evidence.excerpt: I usually lay out two or three reasonable options and ask what matters to them.
evidence.patientFacing: Amy explains the trade-offs of two or three options before agreeing on a plan with you.
evidence.scenario: A patient strongly prefers a treatment you do not initially recommend.

evidence.excerpt: I want people to leave knowing why we chose the plan.
evidence.patientFacing: Amy explains the reasoning behind each recommendation before you leave.
evidence.scenario: A patient asks why you're recommending a particular plan.

evidence.excerpt: I don't treat ADHD in isolation; sleep and mood are part of the same plan.
evidence.patientFacing: Amy works through ADHD, sleep and mental health in one plan rather than as separate problems.
evidence.scenario: A patient comes in about ADHD medication but mentions poor sleep and stress.

evidence.excerpt: If it doesn't fit neatly, we work through it over a few visits.
evidence.patientFacing: Amy is comfortable working through several overlapping issues over a few visits.
evidence.scenario: Symptoms don't fit a clear diagnosis after the first visit.

evidence.excerpt: I'd rather be clear than vague.
evidence.patientFacing: Amy tells you plainly what she thinks is going on.
evidence.scenario: You need to tell a patient a test result isn't what they hoped.

evidence.excerpt: If we change something, I book a review before they go.
evidence.patientFacing: Amy books a follow-up before you leave when a plan changes.
evidence.scenario: What happens between appointments for your ongoing patients?

evidence.excerpt: We talk about routine and sleep as much as medication.
evidence.patientFacing: Amy builds sleep and routine changes into the plan.
evidence.scenario: A patient's main issue seems linked to sleep, exercise and routine.
